messages:
emma_customer: Hey team — we're getting a flood of 429s starting ~10:30 UTC when calling rwd-3-large with ~45k context windows. Not all requests fail, looks bursty. Any idea?
lia_support: Thanks for the flag — can you paste the exact request payload + headers (no secrets)? Also how many parallel clients/threads?
emma_customer: sending stripped example: `POST /v1/generate` header: `Authorization: Bearer X`, `x-client-id: payment-service` body: context ~45k tokens, temperature 0.2. We have 8 worker threads, each batch prefetches up to 4 contexts.
lia_support: got it. Initial suspicion: per-model RPM/TPM and concurrency + large-context path can trigger throttling. i'll loop in infra. @igor_eng can you weigh in on model-specific limits for rwd-3-large?
igor_eng: ping — rwd-3-large has soft RPM/TPM protection and a hard concurrency cap. Typical defaults: 120 requests/min (RPM) per key per model, 150k tokens/min (TPM) aggregated, and 80 max concurrent requests for hosted. Large contexts (>=32k) also reduce effective concurrency because each request holds GPU slots longer.
mario_sre: adding: burst windows are 10s; if you fan out simultaneous prefetches it looks like a spike even if average RPM is low. The queueing will return 429 when the token/TPS budget is exhausted during the burst.
emma_customer: our telemetry shows spikes of 40 reqs in a 6s window due to prefetch across 8 workers. so that matches. Is there a way to avoid 429s without changing lots of client code?
lia_support: options: 1) stagger prefetches/randomize start jitter; 2) reduce prefetch concurrency (e.g., from 4 to 1-2); 3) upgrade to Dedicated plan or request a quota bump; 4) use a smaller model variant for background prefetching.
emma_customer: do you have a quick repro we can run to confirm?
igor_eng: here's a stress repro you can run locally (remove creds):
```
# simple fanout repro
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","input":"<45k context>","temperature":0.0}' &
done
wait
```
This should produce 429s quickly if you hit the burst window.
lia_support: also share how you handle 429s — exponential backoff with jitter is advised. Example header `Retry-After` may not always be present for short bursts.
emma_customer: we currently do immediate retries x3 with 200ms backoff. that's probably too aggressive.
mario_sre: yep — reduce retries and use exponential backoff up to ~2s with randomized jitter. Also, watch token consumption per minute — embedding/cleanup requests count toward TPM.
emma_customer: curious — can you confirm whether long context affects RPM vs TPM accounting? We assumed only tokens matter.
igor_eng: both matter. RPM counts raw requests; TPM counts tokens consumed. Large contexts can push you over TPM quickly; but long requests also hold concurrency slots longer which can trigger concurrency limits even if RPM/TPM are under.
lia_support: i've checked your org logs (emma_customer) — during the 10:30 spike TPM peaked near 210k and concurrent inflight requests touched 92 for rwd-3-large. that's over the default hosted hard cap.
emma_customer: 92 concurrent — ouch. ok. We can throttle prefetching. Any telemetry tips to detect this early programmatically?
mario_sre: instrument average inflight per model + rolling tokens/min. If inflight > 60 sustained, start shedding prefetch. Add alerts for 95pct slowdowns and increased 429 rate.
emma_customer: is there an API response body we can check to differentiate TPM vs concurrency 429? They look the same to us.
igor_eng: current 429 body includes `code: rate_limit`, `hint: "concurrency"` or `hint: "token_quota"` for most cases. If you don't see hint, correlate `Retry-After` or check server-side logs we provided in the support bundle.
lia_support: I've attached a trace id in logs we sent earlier (`trace: rwd-support-247123/a7f3`) — use that when engaging infra.
emma_customer: thanks. if we move to Dedicated, what's the guidance — do you still recommend backoff?
igor_eng: yes — Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and higher concurrency caps but you should still implement backoff and jitter. For Dedicated we can provision higher per-model concurrency (configurable) and bump RPM/TPM depending on commit.
emma_customer: one more — we sometimes prefetch 64k contexts for cold-start cache fills. Does context length beyond 32k have different throttles?
mario_sre: above 32k we route to the extended-context pool which has separate capacity and stricter per-tenant concurrency to protect multi-tenant GPUs. That pool also consumes more TPM quickly. If you rely on 64k often, Dedicated or private deployment is recommended.
emma_customer: great, that explains it. We'll reduce prefetch parallelism, add jitter, and consider Dedicated. Can you confirm a safe initial config (per-worker)?
lia_support: recommended quick change: prefetch_max=1, add jitter rand(0..1000ms) before each prefetch, retry strategy exponential backoff base 300ms cap 3000ms, reduce worker threads from 8 -> 4. Keep an eye for 429s and token/min.
emma_customer: implementing now, will report back in ~1 hour. thanks everyone :pray: 
opsbot: Note: support ticket 12478 updated — assigned to eng for quota/bump evaluation.
sam_platform: tagging billing/qa — if they want Dedicated estimate or short-term quota bump, open a billing request with usage graphs and expected sustained TPM.
lia_support: thanks — i'll follow up with a short runbook and the repro script.
emma_customer: update: after change we see 429 rate drop to near zero during the window. thanks team!
